why: I compared the example values in builder step 2 with the verifier's probe inputs and expected outputs. They overlap. The builder brief lists "padLeft('42', 5, '0') === '00042', padLeft('42', 5) === '   42', padLeft('12345', 3, '0') === '12345', padLeft('abc', 3, '0') === 'abc'". Verifier Check 1 probes p('42',5,'0') and p('42',5) and expects "00042" and "   42". Check 2 probes padLeft('abc',3,'0') and padLeft('12345',3,'0') and expects "abc" and "12345". So the builder gets four of the verifier's exact input/output pairs, which means part of the checker's probe set leaks into the builder brief. The builder's README step ("check that every function exported from index.js has its own ## heading") is also close to Check 3's PASS condition. The overlapping example values alone are enough to break the criterion.
